name: John Rawls
summary: Rawls defended equal basic liberties, fair opportunity and institutions improving the position of the least advantaged. His mature theory favoured dispersed productive wealth or liberal socialism over welfare capitalism. Internationally, he combined assistance and qualified non-intervention with toleration of decent non-liberal societies.

notes: Later pass to rules 7 (2026-11-12). The third-party upload of the Restatement (pdfcoffee) was removed from the evidence: its answers were re-sourced to Political Liberalism (read in the local library) and A Theory of Justice, or nulled with a talk-page record. The Law of Peoples scan was OCR'd again and searched for the war, immigration and toleration passages. The 1995 Dissent essay was not re-read in this pass, so its answers moved to the Law of Peoples section 14.1, which sets out the same principles. Themes searched: economy, government (constitution, courts, majority rule, campaign finance), society (family, gender, religion), world (war, toleration, intervention, aid), liberty, ecology. No position was found on immigration by race, ethnic removal, the parliamentary road to socialism, abolishing wage labour or former empires. Decent hierarchical regimes are objects of international toleration, not his domestic ideal. Open institutional questions stay qualified. Property ownership does not settle women's inheritance specifically. His stationary-state arguments do not establish a particular climate policy.
